author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected on the same form the booking used, prefilled with what is recorded. The correction replaces that visit's details in place and returns to the owner's record; it is checked against the booking rules. The form has no visible entry point (NG-10). Cancelling a visit stays out of scope (NG-5).
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction form shows that visit's recorded date and description.
Submitting a description and a date later than today leaves that visit carrying the submitted date and description, and the owner's record is shown.
An accepted correction leaves the pet with the same number of visits as before the correction.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
Edge case 3: correcting a visit through a pet that does not belong to the named owner, or through a pet the visit does not belong to, is refused.
Edge case 4: a visit whose date has passed cannot be corrected — the future-date rule applies to a correction as it applies to a booking.
non_goals: A link to the correction form from the owner detail page or any other page (NG-10) — deferred to a follow-up request
Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
Any record of a visit's earlier values; the correction overwrites in place
A new confirmation wording for an accepted correction — open question; a new message key would owe eleven translations under REQ-LANG-002
notes: Docs already updated by this dispatch: PRD Visits section (REQ-VIS-003, edge cases 3-4), NG-5 narrowed, NG-10 added, four open questions, and docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md (2026-08-08 non-goal ADR status amended to name the narrowing). OUT OF MY WRITE SCOPE: the ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md still needs a row for 2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md — system-design-expert owns that file. No ubiquitous-language change needed: 'correct' is the PRD's established verb for forward-only amendment (REQ-OWN-004, REQ-PET-004) and Visit is already defined. Three open questions were taken at the narrowest reading rather than blocking: past-dated visits are not correctable, no confirmation wording, earlier-visits list on the form unchanged. IntelliJ MCP semantic-oracle tools (idea, goland) failed to connect this session; PRD authoring used native read/search only, so file_targets are grep-derived and best-effort. Note for design: the existing VisitControllerTests use MockitoBean, which conflicts with the project's no-mocks testing policy; the new tests should follow docs/testing-principles.md, not the surrounding file.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the established nested-edit shape without changing the durable model. system-design.md Overview and Contracts already record the load-bearing invariant this slice depends on: Owner is the aggregate entry point, Pet and Visit are persisted only by cascade from Owner, and no PetRepository or VisitRepository exists. The slice adds a second route pair (GET/POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit) to VisitController, mirroring PetController's /pets/{petId}/edit pair, and makes the existing @ModelAttribute("visit") factory id-aware exactly as PetController.findPet is petId-aware. The one small adjustment is an aggregate accessor: Pet.getVisit(Integer id), mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id). Basis is grep plus full reads of VisitController, Owner, Pet, Visit, BaseEntity, PetController and createOrUpdateVisitForm.html; the IntelliJ oracle was unavailable this session, so this is the weaker resolution basis.
integration_points: VisitController gains initUpdateVisitForm (GET) and processUpdateVisitForm (POST) on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; both reuse the existing view name pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm

loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId and returns the aggregate-resident Visit when present, else the existing new-Visit-plus-addVisit behavior; the @ModelAttribute runs for every mapping in this controller, so this is the single place the two paths diverge
Pet.getVisit(Integer id) traverses pet.getVisits() and is the only lookup path; no VisitRepository is introduced, which preserves the no-repository-below-the-root invariant

the template needs no change: the form carries no th:action so it posts to the current URL, the heading and the previous-visits rows already branch on visit['new'], and minVisitDate is already a controller-wide @ModelAttribute
owners.save(owner) stays the single write; the correction path must not call owner.addVisit(petId, visit)

patterns.description: findPet: form-backing @ModelAttribute made id-aware via an optional @PathVariable, returning the aggregate-resident instance for the edit path and a fresh instance for the create path. Copy this shape for loadPetWithVisit.

updatePetDetails: the project's in-place-update idiom — mutate the instance already resident in the aggregate, then save the root. Note PetController must copy field-by-field because findOwner and findPet each issue their own findById, so the bound Pet is from a different graph. VisitController loads once and puts owner, pet and visit into the model from one graph, so binding already mutates the resident Visit and no copy step is needed.
getPet(Integer id): identity traversal within the aggregate. Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors it.
shouldAddNewVisitForPet: the @DataJpaTest precedent against real H2 for asserting visit-collection cardinality. The in-place counterpart belongs here.

risks.risk: THE LOAD-BEARING ONE — a second visit row is inserted. Pet.visits is @OneToMany(cascade = ALL) with no orphanRemoval, so owners.save(owner) merges the whole collection and any element carrying a null id is treated as transient and INSERTed. The naive failure is not in the handler but in the model-attribute method: if loadPetWithVisit keeps doing new Visit() plus pet.addVisit(visit) unconditionally, it runs for the edit GET and POST too, so the graph already holds a blank extra Visit before the handler executes — the pet gains a row even when the handler correctly updates the existing visit, and the edit form renders blank instead of prefilled.
risks.mitigation: Make loadPetWithVisit branch on visitId and return the resident Visit found through Pet.getVisit(visitId) without adding anything to the collection. Let data binding mutate that instance, then owners.save(owner); the merge issues an UPDATE and the set cardinality is unchanged.

risks.risk: Constructing a replacement Visit and setting its id does not overwrite the existing element. BaseEntity declares no equals/hashCode, so the LinkedHashSet<Visit> in Pet de-duplicates by JVM identity only: a second instance with the same id is a distinct element, yielding a two-element collection and a nondeterministic merge.
risks.mitigation: Never construct a Visit on the correction path. Mutate the resident instance only.

risks.risk: Remove-then-add as a replacement strategy silently orphans data. There is no orphanRemoval and the association is unidirectional via @JoinColumn(pet_id); the h2 schema declares visits.pet_id nullable, so removing the visit from the set writes UPDATE visits SET pet_id = NULL rather than failing loudly, leaving a dangling row.
risks.mitigation: Do not remove from the collection. In-place mutation only; deletion is closed by NG-4.

risks.risk: Identifier smuggling through the form. The visit id must come from the path, never the request body.
risks.mitigation: Leave @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") exactly as it is. Do not relax it to make the id round-trip through a hidden field — the disallow is what makes the mutate-the-resident-instance approach mandatory, and it is the mitigation recorded in system-design.md Threat Model for mass assignment.

risks.risk: Validation drift between booking and correction. @NotBlank on Visit.description comes free with @Valid, but the future-date rule is not a bean-validation constraint — it is a manual result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") in processNewVisitForm (VisitController:100-102). A correction handler that omits it silently accepts a past date, breaching acceptance criteria 5 and edge case 4.
risks.mitigation: Extract the check into one private helper called by both handlers (a TDD Refactor step, not a separate slice). Do NOT replace it with @Future on Visit.date: the Visit() constructor defaults the date to tomorrow, and @Future would change the error code away from typeMismatch.visitDate, whose message key is translated in all eleven bundles — a new key would owe eleven translations under REQ-LANG-002.

risks.risk: Edge case 3 (pet not under the named owner, or visit not under the pet) becomes an IDOR if the visit is fetched by id alone.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing owner -> pet -> visits. Containment is then enforced by construction, with no extra check to forget. Match the existing refusal shape: loadPetWithVisit already throws IllegalArgumentException when the pet is not the owner's; throw the same for a visitId absent from that pet.

risks.risk: A mocked @WebMvcTest cannot observe the criterion that matters. With @MockitoBean OwnerRepository, save() records an argument and proves nothing about persisted rows, so the merge semantics above are invisible and a broken implementation passes.
risks.mitigation: Put the cardinality-and-values assertion where real SQL runs: a ClinicServiceTests case mirroring shouldAddNewVisitForPet (owner 6 / pet 7 already has two seeded visits), and drive the web-layer cases through @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc against real H2 rather than extending the MockitoBean file. testing-principles.md Mocking Policy sanctions the MockMvc harness and calls framework stubs tolerated-not-encouraged. Inside a @Transactional test, flush and clear (or re-find through the repository) before asserting, or the assertion reads the same in-memory instance and passes without any SQL.

risks.risk: Confirmation wording. The booking path sets a hard-coded English flash attribute ("Your visit has been booked"), which would be wrong wording for a correction, and a new key owes eleven translations — listed as an open question in the PRD and taken at its narrowest reading.
risks.mitigation: Set no flash attribute on the correction path; redirect only. The submit button keeps reading #{addVisit} on the correction form for the same reason — a cosmetic wart accepted with NG-10, not a defect to fix in this slice.

notes: No conflict: the 2026-08-27 non-goal ADR records the owner decision narrowing NG-5, and the 2026-08-08 ADR's status names the narrowing, satisfying the reopening condition that ADR set. No docs/adr/README.md gap remains — the index row for 2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md was added by this dispatch, and the 2026-08-08 row's Status cell was updated to match its file. docs/system-design.md deliberately NOT changed: the durable cross-feature model (Owner as aggregate entry point, cascade-only persistence for Pet and Visit, controller-resident business rules) is unchanged by this slice, and that document states current state of the code, so pre-writing REQ-VIS-003 would make it untrue before the slice lands. Owed after the slice lands, as bookkeeping: the Implements cells for the Visit, Pet and VisitController rows gain REQ-VIS-003, VisitController's Purpose becomes booking and correction, and the State Machine paragraph's mention of pet workflows branching on isNew() extends to the visit correction path. file_targets in the prd-entry named Owner.java; the natural home for the traversal is Pet.java (Pet owns the visits collection) and Owner.java likely needs no change — Owner.addVisit is not used by the correction path. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. No ADR is warranted for this slice: the decision is an application of an existing pattern, not a hard-to-reverse trade-off.

findings.description: The diff extends loadPetWithVisit's Javadoc prose (the new correction-vs-booking paragraph) but the @param/@return tags underneath were already stale before this change (only '@param petId' is documented) and the diff adds a fourth parameter (visitId) without adding its tag, so the doc block now documents 1 of 4 parameters and omits @return entirely. findings.fix: Add @param tags for ownerId, petId, visitId, and model, and a @return tag describing that a booking returns a new transient Visit and a correction returns the aggregate-resident Visit.

findings.description: shouldUpdateVisitInPlaceForPet calls pet7.getVisit(visitId) twice in separate assertThat() calls to check description then date. testing-principles.md's assertion guidance (and this skill's checklist) prefers chaining assertions on the same object over repeating the lookup. This is the only instance of the pattern in the changed test surface (the two call sites in VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests.java each look up a different logical value in a single assertThat, so they don't repeat).
findings.fix: Bind the lookup once (e.g. `Visit corrected = pet7.getVisit(visitId);`) and chain `assertThat(corrected.getDescription())...` / `assertThat(corrected.getDate())...`, or combine into one assertThat with two chained matchers.

approved_aspects: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id) exactly in null-return contract, isNew() filtering, and Javadoc phrasing, so the codebase's identity-traversal idiom stays consistent

loadPetWithVisit's booking/correction branch is a clean early-return, avoids constructing a second Visit, and confines correction lookups to the owner->pet->visits traversal (no separate repository), matching the aggregate-only-access invariant
rejectDateNotInTheFuture is a well-placed private helper shared by both handlers, preventing the future-date rule from drifting between booking and correction

VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests.java uses real H2 via @SpringBootTest/@AutoConfigureMockMvc/@Transactional with explicit flush/clear before assertions, correctly avoiding the false-pass risk of asserting against in-memory instances after a merge
Test constant naming (OWNER_WITH_A_BOOKED_VISIT, PET_WITH_A_BOOKED_VISIT, etc.) is descriptive and self-documenting, consistent with three-tier data naming
checkFormat passes with no formatting violations in the changed files

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization is enforced by construction, not by trust in a single id: loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:69-96) resolves owner via owners.findById(ownerId), then pet via owner.getPet(petId), then visit via pet.getVisit(visitId). Every step traverses the loaded aggregate, so a visit can only be reached through the owner and pet named in the path. There is no findById on a visit and no VisitRepository, so the IDOR shape (fetch by visitId alone) is structurally absent.

Cross-aggregate mismatch fails closed before any handler body runs. Because the checks live in the @ModelAttribute factory, both the GET and the POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit abort with IllegalArgumentException before binding, validation or owners.save. No other owner's visit data reaches the model or the view, and no cross-aggregate write is possible. Both containment dimensions are pinned by tests, and across both verbs: pet-not-of-owner on the GET (VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests.java:135-143) and visit-not-of-pet on the POST (:145-152).

Refusal discloses nothing. The IllegalArgumentException carries only the ids the caller itself supplied; it surfaces as the generic 500 page (messages.properties error.500), and server.error.include-message is not enabled anywhere in application*.properties. Both refusal branches throw the same message shape, so there is no existence oracle distinguishing 'no such visit' from 'someone else's visit'.

Mass assignment is closed on the new path. @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") is untouched (VisitController.java:51-54), and the visit id enters only as a path variable. Reparenting is impossible independently of the binder: Visit (Visit.java) exposes only date and description -- it carries no petId or owner property -- and the correction path never calls owner.addVisit, so a client cannot move a visit between pets. Pet.getVisit skips transient rows (!visit.isNew()), so a null-id element cannot be matched and re-bound.

No new model or template exposure. loadPetWithVisit puts the same 'pet' and 'owner' attributes the booking path already put, and pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged and reached by both routes. All user-derived values render through th:text / th:value (Thymeleaf auto-escaping); there is no th:utext, no inlined JavaScript, and no th:action, so the form posts back to the same authorization-checked URL. The 'Previous Visits' table shows the same pet's own visits already visible on the booking form and the owner page.

Redirect target is not attacker-controlled: 'redirect:/owners/{ownerId}' expands the int-typed path variable, so a non-numeric value fails conversion with a 400 before the handler; no open-redirect surface.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle and gradle/ are not in the change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only), so no dependency was added, removed or version-bumped and there is no new CVE surface to verify for this slice.
No secrets introduced: a case-insensitive sweep of the full diff for password/secret/token/api-key/credential/private-key returns nothing.
notes: Scope note, not a finding for this slice: the pre-existing '@ModelAttribute Owner owner' handler parameter means request parameters bind to the loaded Owner before owners.save(owner) on both the booking POST and the new correction POST, so an unrelated owner field could be rebound in the same request. This is the upstream PetClinic shape, present verbatim on processNewVisitForm before this change, and it confers no privilege gain in an application that documents having no authentication or authorization on any route (docs/system-design.md Security Context) and already exposes /owners/{id}/edit to every caller. Recorded so a future security posture change (adding auth) revisits it; nothing to fix here. Reviewed at the planned checkpoint: the threat-model walk completed and the supply-chain check completed, so this is a complete review, not a partial record.

Traced the reasoning against VisitController.processUpdateVisitForm: loadPetWithVisit resolves the visitId-carrying request to the aggregate-resident Visit via the new Pet.getVisit(Integer), and processUpdateVisitForm never calls owner.addVisit, so the invariant the test protects is real and the test would fail if that call were reintroduced (would grow pet.getVisits() to size 2 after flush+clear).

The two refusal-path tests correctly use entityManager.clear() without a prior flush() so they read what Hibernate actually persisted rather than the discarded in-memory mutation the failed binding left on the managed entity — sound technique given binding writes directly onto the JPA-managed Visit returned by the @ModelAttribute factory.

Edge case 3's two halves (pet not owned by owner; visit not owned by pet) and edge case 4 (date not in the future) each have a dedicated, correctly named test matching prd.md's Visits edge-case list verbatim.

All five REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criteria (prefill, in-place replacement, unchanged cardinality, blank-description refusal with field name, non-future-date refusal with field name) have a directly corresponding test.

VisitControllerTests.java (booking path, @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean) is untouched and still exercises only the visitId==null branch of loadPetWithVisit via /visits/new, so it remains valid after the signature change; no gap opened by the new visitId parameter.
JaCoCo shows VisitController.java at 96% (6/150 missed) and Pet.java at 100% line coverage, well above the 80% domain/core target in testing-principles.md.
Three-tier data naming is followed throughout the new integration test (OWNER_WITH_A_BOOKED_VISIT, PET_WITH_A_BOOKED_VISIT, etc. are named by role, no bare literals for ids).

author: change-grader
summary: correct a booked visit in place

blast_radius.note: Nine files, but the production change is 84 lines in two files of one package: VisitController gains a GET/POST pair on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit and Pet gains a getVisit(Integer) traversal. No sensitive paths, no build, schema, config or dependency change, and the Thymeleaf template is untouched. The new mutating route joins the same unauthenticated family the app already exposes at the owner-edit and pet-edit addresses, so it is not a step change in exposure. Five of the nine changed files are docs.

semantic_surprise.note: Three documents state that a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected: prd.md Visits edge case 4, the matching PRD open question ('a visit that has already happened cannot have its description fixed'), and the Consequences section of docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md. The code enforces only that the SUBMITTED date be in the future (rejectDateNotInTheFuture, VisitController.java:161-165); nothing consults the visit's recorded date, and initUpdateVisitForm renders the form for any visit of the pet. The slice's own happy-path tests demonstrate the opposite of the documented rule: pet 7's seeded visits are dated 2013-01-01 and 2013-01-04 (db/h2/data.sql:50,53), and both theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheDetailsInPlace and theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet correct that 2013 visit to LocalDate.now().plusWeeks(1) and assert success. So a past visit's description CAN be fixed, and the side effect is that fixing it silently reschedules a historical clinic record into the future. That is a product question, not a typo. A second, smaller surprise: on a refused correction the form re-renders and the Previous Visits table iterates pet.visits, which now holds the very instance binding just mutated, so the earlier-visits row shows the rejected input rather than the recorded values. Cosmetic, unpersisted (open-in-view is false and no save runs on the refusal path), and untested. The load-bearing constraint itself is sound: loadPetWithVisit early-returns the aggregate-resident Visit without touching the collection, owner.addVisit is never called on the correction path, and the owner-to-pet-to-visit traversal makes containment structural.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real and would fail against a broken implementation. VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests drives the actual web stack against seeded H2 with no repository stub, and the load-bearing case captures the visit count before the correction, flushes and clears the persistence context, then re-reads, so reintroducing owner.addVisit would grow the collection and fail it. The two refusal tests deliberately clear WITHOUT flushing so the assertions read the row rather than the discarded in-memory mutation, which matches production where the graph is detached. ClinicServiceTests.theVisitShouldBeUpdatedInPlaceForThePet pins the same invariant one layer down at the merge boundary. Minor untested edges: nothing asserts the expanded redirect target, the deliberate absence of a flash message on the correction path, or any rendering of the earlier-visits list.

reviewer_hedging.note: No reservations survive. Round one produced three findings, all tagged autofix and all fixable: two from code-quality (stale Javadoc tags on the changed signature, a repeated lookup in a test) and one from test-review (a test name in the pre-BDD style, carrying bar_clause tested-as-spec). The fix round applied all three and both dissenters re-approved on the fix-delta with verification rather than assertion, test-review confirming the renamed method actually executed in the JUnit XML and that binding the repeated lookup into a local preserved the invariant. Security and doc approved in round one with empty findings lists. Security's mass-assignment note is explicitly scoped as the pre-existing upstream model-attribute Owner shape present verbatim on the booking POST, recorded against a future auth posture, not a reservation about this change.

scope_deviation.note: The diff is exactly the triaged surface: two routes, one aggregate accessor mirroring Owner.getPet, the future-date helper extracted from the booking handler so the two paths cannot drift, two test files, and the NG-5 narrowing plus NG-10 documentation that is the product decision this slice implements. Zero build retries and zero consultations. The one design revision was not scope drift: the abort at ledger line 7 was an autofix-audit path-coverage gap over two design-doc files edited by an earlier dispatch, resolved by a superseding design-block with corrected supporting_paths, with the code untouched across the round trip. NG-10 is honored, no page links to the new form.

rationale: The docs say a past-dated visit cannot be corrected; the code only requires the submitted date be in the future, and the slice's own tests correct the seeded 2013 visit to next week and assert success. Read that hunk and decide whether rescheduling a historical visit is intended, then fix the code or the three documents. Everything else is contained and well tested.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected on the same form the booking used, prefilled with what is recorded. The correction replaces that visit's details in place and returns to the owner's record; the submitted date and description are checked against the booking rules. The form has no visible entry point (NG-10). Cancelling a visit stays out of scope (NG-5).
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction form shows that visit's recorded date and description.
Submitting a description and a date later than today leaves that visit carrying the submitted date and description, and the owner's record is shown.
An accepted correction leaves the pet with the same number of visits as before the correction.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
Edge case 3: correcting a visit through a pet that does not belong to the named owner, or through a pet the visit does not belong to, is refused.

Edge case 4 (CORRECTED): a correction is refused when the submitted date is not later than today, whatever date the visit currently carries; a visit whose date has already passed is therefore correctable, and correcting it moves that visit to a future date.
non_goals: A link to the correction form from the owner detail page or any other page (NG-10) — deferred to a follow-up request
Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
Any record of a visit's earlier values; the correction overwrites in place
A bar on correcting a visit whose recorded date has passed — explicitly NOT a requirement; the future-date rule constrains the submitted date only
A new confirmation wording for an accepted correction — open question; a new message key would owe eleven translations under REQ-LANG-002
notes: SUPERSEDES the prd-entry at line 3; corrective dispatch on the change-grader's semantic-surprise concern (line 29). The grader is right and its rationale holds on my own check: the owner's request constrains the SUBMITTED date ('date in the future') and says the form shows the visit's current date and description without qualification, so barring correction of a past-dated visit would invent product policy wider than the narrowest reading, not narrower. rejectDateNotInTheFuture (VisitController.java:161-165) consults only the submitted date; nothing reads the recorded date; the slice's own passing tests correct pet 7's seeded 2013-01-01 visit to next week. DOCS CORRECTED, CODE UNTOUCHED — no behavior change is requested and none was made: (1) docs/prd.md Visits edge case 4 now states the actual rule; (2) the matching PRD open question is reframed as 'Should correcting a visit whose date has already passed stay possible?', naming the current behavior (and its side effect of rescheduling a historical clinic record into the future) as the reading taken meanwhile; (3) the Consequences section of docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md corrected the same way. Only acceptance criterion 7 changed against line 3; criteria 1-6 are verbatim and already satisfied by the landed code, so this record implies no re-implementation. AUTOFIX AUDIT: no prd-autofix records exist in the log, so the judgement audit is a no-op. AUTOFIX-AUDIT PATH COVERAGE: no new trap. docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md is already a dirty design-doc path covered by the design-block at line 9 (supporting_paths, ts after the last commit), so audit-autofix stays green at 4 dirty paths covered without a further design-block co-sign; docs/prd.md is deliberately outside the dirty scan. The structural hazard the system-design-expert flagged at line 9 persists in general (_covers_path admits only design-doc-autofix and design-block, so a non-goal ADR edit made by me after a commit would be uncoverable by my own prd-entry) — harness-side, nothing to do in this slice. REVIEW: the delta is docs-only and touches two files already in the reviewed set; doc-reviewer should re-review it, since its round-1 approval rested on claims two of these three passages now reverse. No ubiquitous-language change. IntelliJ MCP oracle unavailable; native reads and grep only.

author: doc-reviewer
approved_aspects: Edge case 4 in docs/prd.md now states the rule the code implements: rejectDateNotInTheFuture (VisitController.java:161-165) reads only visit.getDate() from the bound (submitted) form object; it never reads or compares against any previously persisted date. Verified against the seeded data (pet 7's visit dated 2013-01-01, db/h2/data.sql:50) and the slice's own passing integration test, which corrects that seeded 2013 visit to LocalDate.now().plusWeeks(1) and asserts a 3xx redirect — the corrected PRD text ('a visit whose date has already passed is therefore correctable, and correcting it moves that visit to a future date') matches this exactly.

docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md Consequences bullet 3 is corrected the same way and is now consistent with the PRD edge case and with the code; no remaining passage in either file asserts that a past-dated visit cannot be corrected. Swept both files plus docs/system-design.md and docs/adr/README.md for the pattern ('cannot be corrected', 'cannot have its description fixed', 'already happened cannot') — no further instance found; the only surviving 'immutable' language is the 2026-08-08 ADR's historical description of the pre-narrowing state, correctly marked superseded by the 2026-08-27 ADR's own Consequences bullet 1, not a claim about current behavior.

The reframed open question ('Should correcting a visit whose date has already passed stay possible?') is a genuine, non-blocking future product question — it does not gate REQ-VIS-003's independently-stated and already-satisfied acceptance criteria — and it names both the narrow reading taken meanwhile (correction of a past visit is allowed) and the side effect (rescheduling a historical record into the future), matching the ADR's own Consequences wording.

Edge-case numbering is unchanged: edge case 4 stays edge case 4 in both the list and the open-question cross-reference ('edge case 4 of Visits'); no downstream renumbering or re-anchoring occurred. Cross-document coherence holds after the edit: prd.md, the two ADRs, system-design.md, and the code agree on the rule wherever they touch it, and no new contradiction was introduced by the correction itself.
docs/system-design.md carries no claim about which dates block a correction (verified by search), so the corrected PRD/ADR wording introduces no new system-design.md mismatch.

Root-cause noted for the record: my round-1 approval verified the ADR's Consequences claims individually but did not cross-check them against the seeded data and the slice's own test outcomes, which is how the past-dated-visit contradiction escaped; this pass re-verified the corrected claims directly against VisitController.java, Pet.getVisit, db/h2/data.sql, and the integration test rather than against the documents' internal consistency alone.
